register.description: This register defines the revision and functional ID.
This register defines the power IDLE mode.

bitfield.description: IDLE MODE. 0x0: Force-idle mode: local target's idle state follows (acknowledges) the system's idle requests unconditionally, i.e. regardless of the IP module's internal requirements. Backup mode, for debug only. 0x1: No-idle mode: local target never enters idle state. Backup mode, for debug only. 0x2: Smart-idle mode: local target's idle state eventually follows (acknowledges) the system's idle requests, depending on the IP module's internal requirements. IP module shall not generate (IRQ- or DMA-request-related) wakeup events. 0x3: Reserved

register.description: This register controls the enabling and the functionality of this AES core.

bitfield.description: This register controls the enabling and the functionality of this IP. Write0:Request to Disabled and enter into Bypass mode. Read0:Disabled and enter into Bypass mode is active When Disabled, then Bypass mux is enabled which will directly connect the otfa_emif4d ocp hp target port to the ocp hp master port. The OTFA core clock is gated in this mode. Write1:Request to Enabled mode Read1:Enabled mode is active When Enabled, all functionality is enabled and bypass mux will be disabled. Note: The SW most follow the defined programming procedure from switching states. Disable -> Enable and Enable -> Disable. See programming model for more details on the procedures that the SW needs to follow. The hw_disable_ctrl input port driven by Efuse bit will disable the ability for SW to set MasterEnable. hw_disable_ctrl = 1, then MasterEnable will be forced to 0, SW WRT will have no effect, SW will always read back 0. hw_disable_ctrl = 0, then MasterEnable state can get controlled by SW. Note: Optimization MMR should not be changed when MasterEnable is 0, after the first Disable -> Enable phase

This register allows the AES-CTR , GCM , GHASH modes to start the required AES jobs as soon as the RD CMD is passed through OTFA to help hide the AES op latency 0x0: Front End CMD AES start disable, only backend response , Legacy mode 0x1: Front End CMD AES start enabled, when enable only AES-CTR, GCM, and GHASH modes are supported
This register controls shift of mac data to always LSB independent of address. 0x0: Default mode 0x1: Set, for FSS use case, updated Opti flash.
This register defines the MAC size. 0x0: 4-bytes 0x1: 8-bytes 0x2: 12-bytes 0x3: 16-bytes.
This register controls the enable of of the OCP Error Response if a MAC error event occurred. The sys_SResp[1:0] will be drive to 3(Error Response) for data words which had the MAC error.

This register allows the ability to stop any new transactions from getting accepted and allow the current transactions to complete. Note: The otfa_emif has a one deep receive pipe stage, this will allow one new crypto cmd to get accepted before backpressure is asserted. Rules: Wait assertion can occur at any time. Wait de-assertion should only occur when CSTATUS.Busy is cleared SW needs to verify CSTATUS.Busy is cleared before it updates crypto region attributes. Non-Crypto transactions get accepted when Wait is asserted.
This register controls the enable of the MAC cache Rd buffer. 0x0: Disabled 0x1: Enabled
cache evict mode
This register controls the key size used for all AES operations. 0x0: 128 Bit 0x1: 256 Bit

This register defines the static allocation of the AES/GHASH cores to read transactions and write transactions. Adjusted only allowed before the OTFA is enabled for first time or after Enable must use the wait/busy method. 0x0: Read and Write is balanced. 50% of the Cypto cores on the Read Pipe 50% of the Cypto cores on the Write Pipe 0x1: Read optimized 75% of the Cypto cores on the Read Pipe 25% of the Cypto cores on the Write Pipe 0x2: Write optimized 25% of the Cypto cores on the Read Pipe 75% of the Cypto cores on the Write Pipe 0xF-0x3: Reserved

register.description: This is the status register which can be used to fine tune the AES core allocation to the Rd Pipe and Wrt Pipe along with a global activity status. Performance Counters which counts the number of events which causes high latency.

bitfield.description: 0x0: No transactions are active, crypto or non-crypto. 0x1: One or more transactions are active, crypto or non-crypto SW needs to read 2 consecutive 0 with 100ns delay or more between samples to insure the pipe is fully empty
0x0: No crypto transactions are active 0x1: One or more crypto transactions are active. SW needs to read 2 consecutive 0 with 100ns delay or more between samples to insure the pipe is fully empty

Read the number of Rd Pipe full events. The counter increments every clock.event that we have no more rd cores available for a new transaction. Saturates to 0x3FFF. Any Write to CSTATUS reset RdStallEventCnt and WrtStallEventCnt to 0x0.

Read the number of Wrt Pipe full events. The counter increments every clock.event that we have no more wrt cores available for a new transaction. Saturates to 0x3FFF. Any Write to CSTATUS reset RdStallEventCnt and WrtStallEventCnt to 0x0.
